Here's Python code using Altair to create various visualizations of the Seattle weather dataset:

```python
import altair as alt
from vega_datasets import data

# Load the Seattle weather dataset
seattle_weather = data.seattle_weather()

# Display first few rows to understand the data
print(seattle_weather.head())
print(seattle_weather.columns)

# 1. Temperature Range Over Time
temp_range = alt.Chart(seattle_weather).mark_area(opacity=0.3).encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='temp_max:Q',
    y2='temp_min:Q',
    tooltip=['date:T', 'temp_max:Q', 'temp_min:Q', 'weather:N']
).properties(
    width=800,
    height=300,
    title='Seattle Temperature Range Over Time'
)

# 2. Average Temperature by Month
monthly_temp = alt.Chart(seattle_weather).mark_bar().encode(
    x='month(date):O',
    y='mean(temp_max):Q',
    color='month(date):O',
    tooltip=['month(date):O', 'mean(temp_max):Q']
).properties(
    width=600,
    height=300,
    title='Average Maximum Temperature by Month'
)

# 3. Precipitation Over Time
precipitation = alt.Chart(seattle_weather).mark_point(opacity=0.3, size=20).encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='precipitation:Q',
    color='weather:N',
    tooltip=['date:T', 'precipitation:Q', 'weather:N']
).properties(
    width=800,
    height=300,
    title='Precipitation Levels Over Time'
)

# 4. Weather Type Distribution
weather_distribution = alt.Chart(seattle_weather).mark_bar().encode(
    x='count():Q',
    y='weather:N',
    color='weather:N',
    tooltip=['weather:N', 'count():Q']
).properties(
    width=400,
    height=200,
    title='Distribution of Weather Types'
)

# 5. Temperature Heatmap by Month and Year
heatmap = alt.Chart(seattle_weather).mark_rect().encode(
    x='month(date):O',
    y='year(date):O',
    color=alt.Color('mean(temp_max):Q', scale=alt.Scale(scheme='redblue')),
    tooltip=['year(date):O', 'month(date):O', 'mean(temp_max):Q']
).properties(
    width=600,
    height=400,
    title='Average Maximum Temperature Heatmap'
)

# 6. Combined Dashboard
dashboard = alt.vconcat(
    temp_range,
    alt.hconcat(monthly_temp, weather_distribution),
    precipitation,
    heatmap
).resolve_scale(
    color='independent'
)

# Display individual charts
temp_range.display()
monthly_temp.display()
precipitation.display()
weather_distribution.display()
heatmap.display()

# Display combined dashboard
dashboard.display()

# Save charts (optional)
# temp_range.save('temp_range.html')
# dashboard.save('seattle_weather_dashboard.html')
```

If you want a simpler starting example:

```python
import altair as alt
from vega_datasets import data

# Load data
seattle_weather = data.seattle_weather()

# Simple line chart of temperatures
chart = alt.Chart(seattle_weather).mark_line().encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='temp_max:Q',
    tooltip=['date:T', 'temp_max:Q', 'temp_min:Q', 'weather:N']
).properties(
    width=800,
    height=400,
    title='Seattle Maximum Temperature Over Time'
).interactive()

chart.display()
```

Key features of the code:
- Uses `vega_datasets` to load the Seattle weather data
- Creates multiple chart types (area, bar, point, heatmap)
- Includes interactive tooltips
- Shows how to combine charts into a dashboard
- Demonstrates different encoding types (temporal, quantitative, nominal, ordinal)

The dataset contains columns:
- `date`: Date of observation
- `precipitation`: Precipitation in inches
- `temp_max`: Maximum temperature
- `temp_min`: Minimum temperature  
- `wind`: Wind speed
- `weather`: Weather type (sun, rain, snow, etc.)
